brief: A clinic reception with a long oak-slat reception counter with a pale stone top as the central anchor, backed by a wall of oak veneer cabinetry with a glowing under-cabinet strip. The lounge/waiting zone sits in front of and beside the counter, next to a floor-to-ceiling glazed wall onto a garden. It has a grey-beige sofa, two light-wood-framed armchairs, a round oak coffee table on a jute rug and a drum side table. Large-format beige stone-look tiles run throughout. A coved ceiling with a warm LED edge glow, recessed downlights and three cream pendants over the counter give a calm, spa-like light. Potted plants (tall floor plants and small trailing ones on the counter), soft watercolour framed art, magazines and mugs on the tables finish it.

must_have.where: centre-back, long counter facing the waiting area, with the oak cabinet wall behind it
one sofa on the right and one on the left by the window; counts as lounge seating
black task chair behind the reception counter
two by the glazing, one at the right wall, one beside the counter
low oak cabinet at the end of the counter / behind it

concept: A calm, biophilic, spa-like healthcare lounge: pale oak, soft greige textiles and beige stone tile, with warm indirect light and abundant greenery so the space feels welcoming rather than clinical.
relations: Oak slat counter front + warm 2700-3000K LED underglow + pale stone top = glowing, welcoming focal point that leads the eye from the entrance
Large glazed garden wall + plants of many sizes = biophilic, daylit calm; greenery repeats the watercolour art
Greige upholstery + light-oak frames + jute rug + beige tile = low-contrast, soft palette that keeps the room relaxed
Coved ceiling glow + recessed downlights + cream pendants = even, shadow-free ambient light at medium brightness
Generous spacing between seating groups = low density, quiet and private for patients
not_reproducible: People, the monitor, phone and paperwork contents, the outdoor garden view and trees, magazine and mug details, the watercolour art itself, and the textured weave of the jute rug.
